claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Composition adjustments within ±5% of nominal concentrations can modulate the hierarchical heterostructure while retaining it.
Minor composition changes alter local chemical environments and nanoscale interface heterogeneities.
Altered local chemical environments and nanoscale interface heterogeneities influence dislocation dynamics.
Altered local chemical environments and nanoscale interface heterogeneities influence crack propagation.
The composition-dependent microstructural landscape governs Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
Real-time microstructural measurements can provide features for an ML model that predicts Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
Using measured microstructural mediators in ML can avoid computationally intensive simulations and thereby reduce prediction time and cost.
The proposed ML framework will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 15–20% relative to high-fidelity CALPHAD and first-principles approaches.
The proposed ML framework will provide roughly a tenfold efficiency gain.
Model reliability will decline when composition variations exceed ±5% of nominal values.
Model reliability will decline when testing departs significantly from room temperature.
Model reliability will decline under elevated-temperature or dynamic-loading conditions because different deformation mechanisms may prevail.
The numerical accuracy and efficiency estimates are based on trends from prior studies.
A blinded holdout dataset containing mechanical-property measurements not used in training will be used to test the model.
Failure to achieve at least a 15% accuracy improvement over traditional computational methods will falsify the hypothesis.
